application: production React build served by actual Express API
provider: deterministic synthetic candidate adapter; no provider calls
checks: Keyboard kind-only correction preserves the statement, effective date, original source/evidence, and displays old Fact/new Preference revision kinds
Mobile edit-and-confirm changes only kind, preserves model/source provenance, creates separate user confirmation, and shows both historical kinds without horizontal overflow
Ordinary confirmation omits kind and preserves the existing Constraint kind in current record and history
Dismissal omits kind and retains Decision history while excluding the record from active recall
Concurrent owner kind correction rejects the stale revision, refreshes the draft selector to current Constraint, and does not replay the obsolete Preference choice
A failed edit-confirm request keeps the selected kind and unconfirmed revision; explicit retry creates exactly one new confirmation
Fresh authenticated HTTP recall reflects current kinds and omits the dismissed candidate
No browser runtime exceptions or external browser requests

body.statement: For synthetic Aster updates, use short paragraphs.
For synthetic Beryl notes, I prefer concise tables.
For synthetic Elm updates, use bullet lists.
For synthetic Fern notes, prefer numbered steps.
For synthetic Fern notes, prefer numbered steps.

visual_review: All four screenshots inspected. Desktop and mobile correction/edit-confirm controls, current kind, and preserved supporting evidence are visible without horizontal clipping. Historical revision kinds were asserted in the rendered DOM; the detail screenshots show the upper current-record/evidence region, not the scrolled revision-history section.
limitations: Uses synthetic source records and a deterministic in-process candidate adapter with disposable PGlite. No live model, embedding endpoint, native database, MCP host or GPU was exercised.
Fresh owner-authenticated HTTP recall was exercised. Browser external requests were blocked and none were observed.
The deliberately simulated HTTP 503 validates form recovery; the revision conflict came from a real concurrent owner API correction.
